Weekly CBC releases, starting with Linux x86_64

Status: accepted, 2026-10-22. The first public release still requires its own green gate and acceptance record.

MixOS starts with Linux x86_64 binaries built against Ubuntu 24.04's glibc 2.39. Each later architecture or operating system needs its own build, package and install proof before it appears in a release.

All Rust build, test and Clippy work runs on the designated CBC workers at one full source commit. The release build uses a signed Ubuntu 24.04 build root on a CBC worker. The packager runs every shipped binary there, records the source commit and hashes in release.manifest.mx, and refuses a higher glibc floor. Those exact bytes move to a draft GitHub Release; GitHub does not rebuild them. A published release is immutable.

The full gate is a distinct commit status, mixos/weekly-x86_64-full. It runs for a frozen weekly candidate after the first release. Normal pushes do not launch a full GitHub-hosted Rust build. A failed gate cannot create a publishable candidate, and the last published version remains current. Any cheaper source checks must use their own status name and cannot stand in for the full gate.

mixos-desktop and mixos-server have separate package membership and acceptance. A desktop candidate may pass while a server service still needs admission. The release notes state exactly which archives are accepted.

The canonical system installation is /opt/mixos. A privileged Mix gold installer verifies the published manifest and archives, records a receipt, and supports rollback. It does not activate running sessions. Prefs and releasesd currently offer verified per-user application installs; their MixOS entries do not update /opt/mixos. A system update control in Prefs must use a reviewed native privilege and activation path before it can claim to update the system.
